intro.summary: Pick a task to find the relevant class, a short example, and the source code. Start with a small project and add LIMEN features as you need them.
desktop.heading: Windows, displays, and data
desktop.body: This standalone Main.hx prints the displays and system theme to the terminal, then writes a sample high score. Build it with the same build.hxml as your first window. It needs no graphics module.
desktop.more: Paths.preference returns a per-user directory path with a trailing separator. The example overwrites record.txt. To load your game's high score, first check that the file exists with sys.FileSystem.exists. Use Window, MessageBox, and FileDialog for the interface. You can set the window icon from an ICO file with window.setIconFile.

input.heading: Keyboard, mouse, and other input devices
input.body: In the first window example, insert this snippet inside while (Platform.pollEvent(event)), after the close check. Move the mouse or connect a device and watch the events in the terminal.
input.more: Use scanCode for shortcuts and handle TextInput for text entry. Enable relative mouse mode with Mouse.setRelative. Cursor supports system and custom pointers. To read controller state, open a Gamepad using the device ID in event.reference and call close when you're done. Use Joystick for raw axes, buttons, and hats (directional switches).

rendering.heading: Rendering and post-processing
rendering.body: Use GraphicsDriver.None for a system utility. Start with OpenGL for a simple game. For lower-level control, Vulkan and Direct3D have their own APIs for resources, commands, shaders, and pipelines. Availability depends on the OS, graphics driver, and modules you built.
